Password reset and login troubleshooting

Use this guide when a customer cannot sign in to the portal or reports a forgotten password.

Self-service reset

  1. Open the portal login page and choose Reset Password.
  2. Enter the email address linked to the account.
  3. Ask the customer to check inbox and spam for the reset link (valid 24 hours).
  4. After setting a new password, sign in again with the same email.

Common issues

  • No email received: confirm the address, wait a few minutes, then resend once.
  • Link expired: request a new reset email; do not reuse old links.
  • Account locked: after five failed attempts the account locks for 30 minutes. Escalate if the customer still cannot access after that window.

Do not ask the customer for their current password. Escalate to a human agent when the account must be unlocked manually or the email on file is wrong.

How to request a refund or escalate to a human

How to request a refund or escalate to a human

Refunds and account changes always require a human agent. The support bot must not approve refunds or change billing data.

Refund request checklist

  1. Collect invoice or order number, amount, and reason.
  2. Confirm the purchase date (demo policy: refunds within 14 days for unused seats).
  3. Open a ticket with priority High and tag it billing.
  4. Tell the customer that a specialist will reply within one business day.

When to escalate

  • Customer asks for a refund, credit note, or contract change.
  • Security concern or suspected unauthorized access.
  • Issue remains unresolved after two documented troubleshooting attempts.

Escalate politely: acknowledge the request, state that a human will follow up, and avoid promising a specific refund amount or timeline beyond the SLA.
Standard NDA and MSA review checklist

Standard NDA and MSA review checklist

Informative checklist for ops and sales. This is not formal legal advice; final contracts must be reviewed by counsel when terms are non-standard.

NDA — points to verify

  • Mutual vs one-way confidentiality and definition of confidential information.
  • Allowed disclosures (legal compulsion, advisors under confidentiality).
  • Term of confidentiality (demo default: 3 years after disclosure).
  • Return or destruction of materials on request.

MSA — points to verify

  • Scope of services and order-form precedence over the MSA.
  • Limitation of liability and exclusion of consequential damages.
  • Governing law and dispute venue (demo template: Brazil / São Paulo).
  • Termination for convenience and for cause notice periods.

Escalate to legal counsel when the customer redlines liability caps, IP ownership, or data-processing clauses beyond the approved templates.
Data processing and privacy handling notes for quotes

Data processing and privacy handling notes for quotes

Guidance for sales and ops when a prospect asks how personal data is handled in a quote or pilot. Answers are informative only.

Demo processing principles

  • Process only data needed to deliver the quoted service.
  • Do not move customer personal data to personal devices or unmanaged tools.
  • Subprocessors used for hosting/email must appear on the approved list.
  • Retention for demo pilots: delete or anonymize pilot data within 30 days after end, unless a signed order says otherwise.

What sales may say

  • We can share a standard DPA / privacy addendum with the order form.
  • Security questionnaires go to the ops security contact.

What sales must not invent

  • Certifications that are not listed in the approved security one-pager.
  • Custom retention or residency commitments without legal review.

Non-binding proposal and disclaimer guidelines

Proposals and estimates are commercial invitations to negotiate until an order form or signed contract is executed.

Required disclaimer (demo wording)

This proposal is for discussion purposes only and does not create a binding obligation. Prices, timelines and scope are estimates and remain subject to a signed order form and applicable terms.

Rules for sales

  • Always include the disclaimer on PDF proposals and email summaries.
  • Do not state that a proposal “is already approved” or “guarantees” SLAs.
  • Custom legal terms require counsel before the customer signs.

If a prospect treats a proposal as a signed contract, clarify politely and route the signature package through the standard order-form process.

New customer onboarding SOP (internal)

Internal procedure for ops after a signed order. Do not share this SOP with customers or publish it on the website.

  1. Kick-off: create the project, assign CSM and technical lead within 1 business day of signature.
  2. Environment: provision staging, then production; store credentials in the approved vault only.
  3. Data: import agreed master data; validate with the customer on a shared checklist.
  4. Training: schedule admin training before go-live; record attendance.
  5. Go-live: require written customer confirmation and a completed rollback note.
  6. Handover: move the account to support with open risks documented in the ticket.

Escalate to the delivery manager if kick-off slips more than 3 business days or if production access is requested before the security checklist is done.

Incident triage and internal escalation (internal)

Ops-only runbook for classifying and escalating production incidents.

Triage steps

  1. Confirm impact: number of users, environment (prod/staging), start time.
  2. Assign severity (SEV1–SEV4) using the internal severity matrix.
  3. Open an incident channel and nominate an incident commander.
  4. Capture timeline notes every 15 minutes for SEV1/SEV2.

Escalation path (demo)

  • SEV1: page on-call + notify delivery manager immediately.
  • SEV2: on-call within 15 minutes; manager if unresolved after 1 hour.
  • SEV3/SEV4: standard queue during business hours.

Customer-facing updates go through support using approved status wording. Do not post root-cause speculation in public channels.

Change request approval workflow (internal)

Internal process before applying production changes that affect customer environments or shared infrastructure.

  1. Open a change request with summary, risk, rollback plan, and maintenance window.
  2. Peer review by another engineer (mandatory for production).
  3. Approval: team lead for low risk; delivery manager for high risk or customer-visible downtime.
  4. Execute in the approved window; verify health checks after deploy.
  5. Close the change with outcome and links to commits/tickets.

Emergency changes (SEV1) may proceed with verbal lead approval, followed by a retroactive change record within 24 hours.

Qualification checklist for discovery calls

Use this playbook before writing a proposal. Prefer documented answers over assumptions.

  • Problem: what process or tool is failing today?
  • Impact: users affected, cost of delay, compliance risk.
  • Decision makers: economic buyer, technical evaluator, champion.
  • Timeline: target go-live and hard deadlines.
  • Budget: range confirmed or next step to confirm it.
  • Success metrics: how the customer will measure value after 90 days.

Do not send a priced proposal until problem, decision makers, and timeline are clear. Escalate to a human sales manager for strategic or multi-year deals.

Proposal FAQ — what sales may commit

Proposal FAQ — what sales may / may not commit

Sales may

  • Share list pricing and approved discount bands from the commercial policy.
  • Offer a time-boxed pilot with a written pilot scope.
  • Promise standard onboarding steps listed in the delivery package.

Sales may not

  • Guarantee features that are not on the public roadmap or signed SOW.
  • Promise legal language changes without counsel.
  • Commit unlimited support or custom SLAs without ops approval.

When unsure, say you will confirm with the deal desk and avoid binding language in chat or email until the order form is ready.

Company overview and product summary

Welcome. This demo company helps mid-size teams run operations, customer support and sales processes on a modern business platform.

What we offer

  • Implementation and configuration of core business apps.
  • Integrations with common accounting, e-commerce and messaging tools.
  • Ongoing support packages after go-live.

For a tailored quote, contact the sales team. For help with an existing account, use customer support after signing in to the portal.
Public FAQ — contact channels and business hours

Public FAQ — contact channels and business hours

How can I reach you?

  • Website livechat: available on this site during business hours.
  • Sales email: sales@example.com (demo address).
  • Support portal: for existing customers after login.

Business hours

Monday–Friday, 09:00–18:00 (America/Sao_Paulo). Messages outside these hours are answered on the next business day.

Do you offer demos?

Yes. Ask for a product demo and a specialist will schedule a call. We do not share internal procedures or customer-only manuals in public chat.

Getting started without an account

Visitors can explore public product information without signing in.

  1. Browse the website FAQ and product overview pages.
  2. Request a demo or pricing conversation via sales.
  3. After purchasing, you receive portal credentials by email.
  4. Use the support portal for account-specific help (password reset, tickets).

If you already have an account but cannot sign in, use the portal password reset or contact support. Livechat for anonymous visitors cannot change account data or process refunds.
